say: Meeting prep for Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd: 2 questions, 1 people to call first.

snapshot.about: Dixon Technologies (India) Limited,  incorporated  in  1993 ,  is  a  Electronic  Manufacturing  Services  (EMS)  company  with operations in the electronic products vertical such as consumer electronics, lighting, home appliance, closed-circuit television cameras  (CCTVs), and mobile  phones. It also  undertakes reverse logistics operations.  Besides, it manufactures security surveillance equipment, wearables & audibles, AC-PCBs. Recently, it has entered a JV with Imagine Marketing Private Limited for designing and manufacturing wireless audio solutions in India.
key_points: a) Mobile & EMS Division (90% in FY26 vs 85% in FY25)
The company has emerged as the
fastest-growing EMS company by revenue and market capitalisation
. It manufactures feature phones, smartphones, IT hardware, Telecom, hearables & wearables. Its key client in this segment includes Samsung.
b) Consumer Electronics & Appliances (6% in FY26 vs 9% in FY25):
The company offers LED TVs (32-98 inches), Smart TVs, Monitors, IFPD Commercial displays, Digital signage PCB & LCM panel assembly, and LED Bar Injection moulding. It is the
largest Original Design Manufacturing (OEM & ODM) company in India
Xiaomi, Samsung, Hisense, Panasonic, Acer, Toshiba, BPL, Lloyd, VU, Motorola, etc.

cash.note: Post-investment cash = CFO + CFI (screener doesn't split capex from treasury moves); treat as a proxy for FCF.

items.quote: So as guided earlier also, we feel that these are high double-digit teen margin businesses for us which, of course, we expect the same to start generating those kind of numbers in next financial year.
items.speaker: Saurabh Gupta
items.why: No quarter reported since this call.

items.quote: Yes, so basically, just to add, Renu, this year we are looking at a volume of closer to 1.3 -1.4 million, which will translate into revenues of closer to INR 6,000-6,500 crores.
items.speaker: Saurabh Gupta
items.why: An absolute or qualitative target — nothing in the quarterly P&L to hold it to.

items.quote: Our market position, customer engagement and manufacturing capabilities remain intact, and we expect 20% to 25% volume growth quarter- on-quarter growth as consumer demand strengthens and we have a strong order book.
items.speaker: Atul Lall
items.why: Revenue QoQ +40.2% next quarter (Sep 2026) vs 20–25% promised.

items.quote: So quarter 2 against quart er 1, we are expecting a 20%, 25% kind of a growth.
items.speaker: Saurabh Gupta
items.why: Revenue QoQ +40.2% next quarter (Sep 2026) vs 20% promised.

items.quote: Over the past few weeks, supply -demand dynamics are becoming more balanced, and we are beginning to see an improvement in customer ordering pattern, and we expect a high -double- digit growth quarter-on-quarter in the smartphones volume along with growth in selling prices by 12% to 15%.
items.speaker: Atul Lall
items.why: Revenue QoQ +47.9% next quarter (Jun 2026) vs 12–15% promised.

items.quote: We feel that it should be double-digit margin.
items.speaker: Atul Lall
items.why: The promise refers back to something said earlier (“it/this”) — open the transcript for context.

items.quote: We are targeting a revenue of almost INR2,500 crores in that business.
items.speaker: Atul Lall
items.why: An absolute or qualitative target — nothing in the quarterly P&L to hold it to.

items.quote: We still feel that we should be able to have a margin of somewhere between 2.8% to 3.1%, 3.2% in our mobile phone business.
items.speaker: Atul Lall
items.why: Segment-level guidance — the consolidated P&L can't confirm it; see the segment note in the results filing.

items.quote: So this year, we feel the revenue should be in the range of INR1,500-odd crores.
items.speaker: Atul Lall
items.why: An absolute or qualitative target — nothing in the quarterly P&L to hold it to.

promises.read: 3 of 3 checkable promises met or on track; analysts kept pressing on demand.

bull: Revenue compounding 58.9% a year over 3 years (accelerating vs 49.9% 5-yr).
Net profit up 86.1% CAGR over 3 years.
